name: masterdns-upstream
mobile_binding: Feasible: pure-Go client core lives under internal/, straightforward gobind wrap into an AAR
notes: Core reference for MasterDNS tunnel type; clean client/server cmd layout.

name: stormdns
mobile_binding: Feasible: independent MIT fork of MasterDnsVPN with same internal/-centric Go structure, AAR-friendly
notes: arq/multi-resolver + v2 tunnel fork; LICENSE covers both original and modifications under MIT.

name: masterdns-qs
license_ok: no LICENSE file and no license statement in README; unknown
mobile_binding: Technically feasible (pure Go, one binary with client/server modes) but legally unbindable until licensing is clarified
notes: Single-binary DNS-uplink/spoofed-UDP-downlink client; warns spoofing may violate provider rules.

name: pingtunnel
mobile_binding: Partially feasible: ships icmp_listen_android.go bridge, but client needs a raw ICMP socket the app must acquire; root-free path unverified
notes: Largest vendored tree; client runs as local proxy, needs privileges investigation before Android binding.

name: spoof-tunnel
mobile_binding: Gomobile not viable: raw-socket spoofing path requires system-level privileges, so ship as an external binary or wrapper
notes: Cobra CLI with local/remote/tester subcommands plus Rust XDP relay and panel backend.

name: balevpn
mobile_binding: Gomobile not applicable: no Go core, binding would be Rust FFI or direct use of the Kotlin app code
notes: Architecture reference: multiple Rust crates (lktunnel, bale, lk-signaling) plus an Android app.

name: qr-tunnel
mobile_binding: Feasible in principle: pure-Go binary, but the LiveKit DataChannel dependency may pull SDK/native bits that complicate gobind
notes: MIT is declared only in README (no LICENSE file must be added upstream before distribution).

name: nooshdaroo
mobile_binding: Gomobile not applicable: Rust crates; use prebuilt NDK-built binaries through FFI
notes: Tiny SOCKS5-over-DNS client, well suited as the binder target; separate client/server/lb crates.

name: qwdtt
mobile_binding: Gomobile technically possible (upstream builds Android native libs) but GPL-3 infects any AAR redistribution
notes: qWDTT Android client + wdtt-server; WireGuard-based (pion dtls, zx2c4 wireguard); GPL gate blocks direct vendoring of AAR.

name: golden-gre
mobile_binding: Gomobile not applicable: C relay and shell scripts are meant to run as compiled binaries on servers
notes: GRE transport used server-side/relay; monocypher vendored inside relay dir.

name: csqtt
mobile_binding: Gomobile not applicable: upstream ships Rust code as a native .so loaded by the Kotlin app (non-Go binding path)
notes: PolyForm Noncommercial is non-allowlisted; commercial use prohibited so needs a separate licensing verdict.

name: olcrtc
license: DO WHAT THE FUCK YOU WANT TO PUBLIC LICENSE v2
mobile_binding: Feasible: pure Go with cmd/olcrtc-cgo wrapper and internal mobile package including VpnService protector hooks
notes: WTFPL is outside the MIT/Apache/BSD/MPL allowlist despite permissive spirit; upstream declares the project effectively EoL.

name: openflux
mobile_binding: Already done upstream: mobile/ package exposes gomobile bindings (Android owns the TUN fd) and build_android.sh exists
notes: GPL-3 blocks AAR redistribution; packet transport over a Yandex document channel.
